OwnerFields:
      title: Owner fields
      description: Editable fields of a pet owner.
      type: object
      properties:
        firstName:
          title: First name

          title: Last name
          description: The last name of the pet owner.
          type: string
          minLength: 1
          maxLength: 30
          pattern: "^[\\p{L}]+([ '-][\\p{L}]+){0,2}\\.?$"
          example: Franklin
        address:
          title: Address
          description: The postal address of the pet owner.
          type: string
          minLength: 1
          maxLength: 255
          pattern: '.*\S.*'
          example: '110 W. Liberty St.'
        city:
          title: City
          description: The city of the pet owner.
          type: string
          minLength: 1

          pattern: '.*\S.*'

          title: Telephone number
          description: The telephone number of the pet owner.
          type: string
          minLength: 1
          maxLength: 20
          pattern: '^[+()\d\s-]+$'
          example: '6085551023'

          type: string
          format: email
          maxLength: 255
          example: george.franklin@example.com

The full build succeeded with all tests green.

## Summary

I implemented the rule *"reject a supplied `registrationDate` later than the server date → 400"* with minimal structural impact.

**Changes (2 files):**

1. **New class** `service/RegistrationDateValidator.java` — a tiny, cohesive unit (no surrounding class complexity) with one static method that throws `IllegalArgumentException` when the supplied date is after `LocalDate.now()`, and passes through `null`/valid dates unchanged.

2. **`mapper/OwnerMapper.java`** — added a single `@Mapping` line routing `registrationDate` through the validator during `toOwner(OwnerFieldsDto)`, matching the existing pattern used for `telephone`, `address`, and `postcode`.

**Why this keeps cost low:** The existing `ExceptionControllerAdvice` already maps `IllegalArgumentException` → 400, so no controller edit was needed — the large `OwnerRestControllerV1` and `Owner` classes (high WMC_other) were left untouched. The only edit is a one-line annotation on an abstract mapper method (CC 1), and the new logic lives in its own class with zero surrounding complexity.

Tests: `AcceptanceTest.errorRejectsFutureDate` passes, full suite `BUILD SUCCESS`.
